prompt: service.log is the API gateway's access log for 32 minutes (~39K tokens). The counting rules live only in limits.yaml, api_keys.txt and exemptions.txt - read all three, comments included (the log records the API key a request was made with, never a tenant; api_keys.txt is the only key -> tenant map, and exemptions.txt scopes each row by tenant AND by key). Several requests in the log violate a rate limit. Write ANSWER.txt in exactly two sections. Section one is the line "# ids", then one line per violating request holding its req= value (8 hex digits), sorted ascending. Section two is the line "# counts", then one "<name> <count>" line for every name with at least one violation, sorted by name: <name> is the tenant of the violating request, or "global" for an id that only the global limit decides. Nothing else, and the counts sum to the number of ids. Use the tools; when you are done, call submit.
trap: one scan of the log grouped by the key it records - no key -> tenant map, no global limit, no exemptions, the named-key exemption row ignored, retired-key 403s, ops maintenance and /health probes all counted: 23 plausible ids of which 8 are real, on per-key rows
